#6651. Grand Theft Auto VI Welcomes a New Wave of (Virtual) Gym Bros

After a 13-year drought, Grand Theft Auto VI has finally hit the masses. Predictably, a large swath of guys have called off work to give themselves just enough time to explore the immersive fictional land of Leonida, where players can do just about everything they can in real life—from driving cars and renovating homes to playing video games within a video game. In Grand Theft Auto VI, that now also includes hitting the gym. And if you want to progress through the story as efficiently as possible, becoming an in-game gym rat might be the best thing you can do.

Expanding on a gameplay mechanic introduced in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, working out in GTA levels up your character to help with progressing through the story. The fitter you become in the game, the more stamina you have to sprint, the more health you have before you’re Wasted, and the more focus you have to take down enemies. Just like in real life, pumping iron makes daily life a whole lot easier.

To get fit, you can use the weights in Jason’s outdoor gym, which features the big three full-body lifts: squats, bench presses, and deadlifts. While your character handles the heavy lifting, all you have to do is carefully time your button presses to complete reps without causing an injury. Once you have enough money, you can purchase memberships at gyms across the city, giving you access to treadmills, free weights, and workout machines. The exercise options are so extensive (you can even do zone 2 cardio) that gamers have already started trading tips to the best GTA 6 workouts for maximizing your character’s gains.

As your character gets stronger, their avatar transforms accordingly, developing more defined muscles, a six-pack, and even a chiseled face. Neglecting your fitness and overeating (a real thing you can do in the game) has an alternate effect as your player visibly gains weight and adopts a “dad bod.”

Inevitably there will be many players that skip the gym this weekend so they can pump a little virtual iron with their thumbs. There’s something undeniably ironic about looksmaxxing your GTA character while spending hours sitting on the couch playing a video game. But don’t think that just because it’s all on a screen that you won’t walk away from a session with a little back pain, so maybe schedule a few breaks in between. You could even build a home gym of your own like Jason’s—it’s already got one fitness expert’s approval.

If it’s your turn to host Thanksgiving or Friendsgiving this year, you have no shortage of themes to choose from, whether elevated, playful, or a little of both. Tableware has become an event in its own right, and the table you set can be as memorable as the meal itself.

And the best part? You don’t need a designer’s budget or a showroom’s worth of serveware to pull it off. Start with what you already own, then layer in a few thoughtful extras: a handful of taper candles, a fall foliage tablecloth, or elevated glassware. The most striking tables this year feel gathered rather than bought, and they leave plenty of room for your own personality to take a seat alongside your guests.

Ahead, our favorite Thanksgiving tabletop themes, curated to help you host your best dinner yet.

A fall foliage tablescape feels warm and inviting, built on rich browns and earthy neutrals. Fall leaves take center stage alongside amber or orange glassware, a leaf-printed tablecloth, and other nature-inspired accents like leaf taper holders, cream-colored placemats, and pinecones tucked between candlesticks.

Stick to a restrained palette of burgundy, stone, and silver, then let texture do the work with textured servers, glossy ceramic plates, and simple white taper candles. Make it feel extra special with handwritten placecards and glass tea light holders. Less really is more here.

#6646. The Las Vegas Grand Prix Kicks Off With a Disco Bash by SkinCeuticals

Outside, the city of Las Vegas is readying its streets for this weekend’s Formula One Grand Prix, when the world’s fastest drivers in the world’s fastest cars will tear down the Strip at 200-plus miles per hour. But inside Sin City’s hot spots, the starry F1 events are just getting started—and everyone at the SkinCeuticals Las Vegas Grand Prix Party quite literally had their (glowing) game faces on.

On Wednesday night, SkinCeuticals, as the official skincare partner of Scuderia Ferrari HP, hosted an exclusive bash at Baby Disco, the intimate, moody lounge tucked away within Zero Bond at The Wynn Las Vegas.

With the space aglow in Ferrari Rosso Scuderia red under a shiny mirrored disco ball and a checkered-flag DJ booth, guests snacked on wagyu bites and gourmet caviar-topped chicken nuggets and sipped on-theme cocktails. (Also served: SkinCeuticals’s top-shelf favorites, including the P-TIOX and C E Ferulic serums, passed around on silver trays.) The model Kelly Piquet, partner of F1 star Max Verstappen, posted up on the green velvet banquette, as other attendees played around with SkinCeuticals-branded poker chips and cards around the room.

On the venue’s outdoor terrace overlooking the glowing marvel that is Sphere, actor Chace Crawford and his dad, dermatologist Chris Wayne Crawford, took a moment to enjoy the view. The two were doing a little father-son bonding—a perfect setting since F1 is “a male, testosterone-fueled sport,” joked Chris. As a Texas native, Chace (who also came through GQ’s Men of the Year 2026 party in LA last week) has seen the F1 Grand Prix in Austin, but he’s excited to catch his first race under the megawatt Vegas lights. “It’s surreal out here,” said the The Boys star, looking out over the Strip.

Inside, sportscaster and former Seattle Seahawk superstar Russell Wilson, a big F1 fan, couldn’t wait for lights-out-and-away-we-go on Sunday. He’s attended F1 races in Monaco and Montreal, but he really digs the Vegas experience. “I’m racing around the track tomorrow night,” he said, “so I’m fired up about it.”

At 9 p.m. the party kicked into high gear as Alex Pall and Drew Taggart of the Chainsmokers took to the DJ booth, easing into their set, kicking off a remix of thesynth-pop classic “Don't You Want Me” then incrementally dialing up the heat until Taggart took to the mic himself to perform “Paris,” the DJ duo’s 2017 hit. When the musician Sooin, of the K-pop group Meovv, hopped into the booth to chop it up with the Chainsmokers, the room lit up.

They closed out their set with some on-theme bottle service, as the Baby Disco crew made their way through the crowd hoisting magnums of Champagne and a strobe-flashing disco ball shaped like SkinCeuticals’s iconic serum dropper bottle. Time for the cooldown lap.

“I just want to say, everyone has really nice skin in here,” Taggart told the room with a grin. “Shout out to SkinCeuticals.”

#6639. 14 Best Barn Coats for Men in 2026, According to GQ Editors

The best barn coats for men are a close cousin of the chore jacket—similar in spirit, but built tougher. They’re heartier, heavier, better insulated, and usually more water-resistant. Where the chore jacket belonged to the factory floor, the barn coat was made for the fields: a layer you could shrug on to tackle chores outdoors.

But ever since the ’80s and ’90s, the barn coat has been finding a new audience of urbanites who understand its utility, even on mean city streets. Today, alongside the waxy Barbour zip-ups and dad-approved L.L. Bean riffs, a ton of capital-F fashion labels—The Row, Auralee, Prada—have been herding the barn coat back into the center of the style conversation.

Reading to buy your first barn coat? Make sure it’s cut with enough room to comfortably slip a sweater beneath it, and that its craftsmanship ensures it’ll remain a reliable rotation beater for years to come. The former, of course, might demand some trial and error on your end, but the latter is exactly where we come in. These are the absolute best barn coats for men on the market right now, from the genre-defining joints you already know to the sleeper-hit versions you probably don’t.

Deep, easily accessed pockets? A warm corduroy collar? A charming plaid lining? This jacket from J.Crew is, quite simply, the platonic ideal of a barn coat. It has all the details dialed in, built upon a sturdy, 100% cotton washed canvas body that will only soften and feel more like your own in time. Originally launched over 40 years ago, there’s a reason J.Crew is still able to sell it four decades later. And we didn’t even mention the hook on the back, so you can hang this up with ease as soon as you enter your bustling, warm, overcrowded local bar. It’s the little things.

I should disclose up front that I’m a bit of an OrSlow obsessive. I own more from the brand than I’ll ever admit publicly or privately and doubt that I’ve ever been unaware of something it’s produced, but this is because no brand has more consistently lived-up to pre-purchase expectations in my illustrious shopping career, and the only things that see the light of day are things that are absolutely dialed. And this jacket is dialed, folks. Made in Japan from start to finish, it has the kind of cut that can handle a Joey Tribbiani-esque volume of layers, is made from a cotton canvas fabric that will look unreal in half a decade, and the type of construction that other brands show factories when they’re trying to describe what they’re looking for.

We couldn’t round out a piece on barn coats without a nod to L.L. Bean, one of the OGs of the style. A century ago, Bean launched a rugged duck-hunting coat that slowly shifted into a catch-all field jacket—the ancestor of the one they’re still selling today. It’s made from hefty, water-resistant canvas, with a sewn-in lining, five roomy pockets, underarm gussets, and bi-swing shoulders so you can actually move in it. And like many things Bean, the sizing is inclusive, there’s even a “Tall” option for the vertically gifted among us.

The Real McCoy’s is known for painstakingly recreating vintage garments—the Abercrombie set that Hunter S. Thompson made famous is an all-timer—so you can bank on the fact that this barn jacket has all the proper credentials. If you are dubious, however, know that it’s made out of a damn-near-bulletproof cotton canvas fabric, is fully lined with twill to trap some heat when things get chilly, has a perfect hit of corduroy at the collar and comes equipped with one of the sickest pocket configurations you’ll ever see in the genre. It’s hard to call anything “perfect,” but I feel comfortable saying that this is an ideal barn jacket, and would be hard to beat against any rubric.

What’s all this, then—a Barbour as a barn coat? The Beaufort isn’t cut from the same stiff American canvas, but the brief is identical: a country jacket for tramping through fields, feeding the chickens, or—let’s be honest—making it to the pub. King Charles even reinstated the brand’s Royal Warrant last year (he is the Menswear King, after all). Built long before DWR and Gore-Tex, its waxed cotton shrugs off rain, the oversize corduroy collar blocks the wind, and you can zip in liners or snap on a hood if you feel like accessorizing. Best detail? The little hand-warmer pockets perched above the main ones—perfect for thawing fingers after a day of grouse shooting or a lap of the Lower East Side. Just remember: it will need the occasional re-waxing, but that’s all part of the fun.

If you're getting hung up on the idea of a barn jacket that’s implicitly unqualified to do barn jacket work, this isn’t going to be the one for you. But you if think that the barn jacket can be both a highly-functional, historically-revered workwear staple AND that it’s a brilliant canvas on which the most tasteful among us can mess around a little, this one from the maniacs (complimentary) at Auralee is hypnotic. The outer is made from a cotton moleskin—which is like flannel’s heavyweight cousin, for those unfamiliar—that’s been unevenly garment-dyed to look like it’s endured thousands of miles on a tractor. Meanwhile, the pockets are flawless, the zipped placket comes outfitted with a buttoned storm flap, and the whole thing is garnished with a detachable shearling collar, just in case you thought they spared a single expense along the way.

Knickerbocker is known for tasteful pieces that can help you rebuild an entire wardrobe, and that includes this faithful homage to vintage fly-fishing wading jackets commonly worn in the jacket’s namesake upstate region. The Portuguese canvas and rounded collar stand out among other jackets on our list, and the gusseted shoulders allow for a wide range of movement on and off the river.

First off, don't fear the red colorway. It's just as easy to wear as any other fall-adjacent color and it stands out roughly twice as much, which is kind of the dream ratio for eye-catching jackets. Also, it's just a damn-good barn coat, with deep ol' hand pockets, a wind-stopping corduroy collar and endless layering potential.

This is absolutely a barn jacket. All the hallmarks are there, from the corduroy collar (more on that later) to the generous pocket situation and layout. But it's also one of the most stunning corduroy jackets on the market due to one of the most breathtaking corduroys you will ever see. And if you ever were wondering, why don't they make the whole jacket out of the collar, they do.

Filson's classic Barn-adjacent coat is an undeniable giant in the space—big ol' stow pockets, corduroy collar, canvas outer—but the insulated iteration is every bit as easy to wear and twice as warm, without adding much bulk at all.

Think of this TS joint as the ultimate "what if." Like, what if, instead of a classic canvas outer there was a super soft, ultra sturdy, almost flannel-like flocked denim? And instead of corduroy, TS threw in a leather collar? Because across the board, they decided to find out.

Much like the Auralee number up top, this isn't the kind of barn jacket that you'd be wearing to bale hay, but there's only a select few among us doing that anyways. You can, however, wear the living hell out of this all winter long, because not only does it layer beautifully, it has the requisite storage, showstopping potential and only gets better with age. Is it practical? That's not the point.

Levi’s takes a no-nonsense swing at the barn jacket—exactly what you’d expect from them. You get a sturdy shell, a quilted lining that brings just the right amount of warmth, and two generous front pockets. Sure, it skips the classic hand-warmer pockets, but at a price this good, you can afford to overlook a detail or two.

This is one of the most affordable options on this list, but you're not leaving a ton on the table if this is your prefered route. The outer is a waxed organic cotton that will hold up well against all forms of precipitation, there's a full flannel lining and the collar even buttons into a stand, to really keep things insulated.

Style is subjective, we know—that’s the fun of it. But we’re serious about helping our audience get dressed. Whether it’s the best white sneakers, the flyest affordable suits, or the need-to-know menswear drops of the week, GQ Recommends’ perspective is built on years of hands-on experience, an insider awareness of what’s in and what’s next, and a mission to find the best version of everything out there, at every price point.

Our staffers aren’t able to try on every single piece of clothing you read about on GQ.com (fashion moves fast these days), but we have an intimate knowledge of each brand’s strengths and know the hallmarks of quality clothing—from materials and sourcing, to craftsmanship, to sustainability efforts that aren’t just greenwashing. GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

To kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

We lean on that collective experience to guide our search, culling a mix of household names, indie favorites, and the artisanal imprints on the bleeding-edge of the genre. Then we narrow down the assortment to the picks that scored the highest across quality, fit, and price.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally new to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

Whatever your preferences, whatever your style, there's bound to be a superlative version on this list for you. (Read more about GQ's testing process here.)

#6634. Who Is Miley Cyrus’s Husband, Maxx Morando?

The couple officially said “I do” in Palm Springs

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are officially married! Nearly one year after their engagement was confirmed, the couple tied the knot on Saturday, November 21, in Palm Springs, California.

The singer, who said “I do” in Saint Laurent, shared black-and-white photos from the wedding on Instagram, simply captioning the post, “M+M 🤍 11.21.26.” In photos, the couple could be seen exchanging vows in a poolside ceremony featuring a stunning display of sweeping white flowers and candles.

In December 2025, Cyrus confirmed her engagement to musician Maxx Morando—a relationship she has largely kept out of the spotlight following her highly publicized marriage to Liam Hemsworth. The Bass Persuades singer was first linked to Morando in November 2021, when the two sparked romance rumors with a joint appearance at the Gucci Love Parade fashion show. (Cyrus later shared a photo of herself with Morando from the event on Instagram.)

Rumors escalated the following month, when Cyrus danced and held hands with Morando in Miami during her New Year’s Eve Party special for NBC. By April 2022, they confirmed their romance during an outing in West Hollywood, where they went all out with the PDA.

Fast forward to the 2024 Grammys and Morando supported Cyrus at the show—where she won her first Grammy for “Flowers”—and he gave her a passionate kiss.

Since then, the two have kept their relationship low-key aside from a few red carpet appearances together. But while Morando has mostly kept his personal life out of the public spotlight, he, like Cyrus, has had a long career in music.

Ahead, everything we know about Cyrus’s new husband, Maxx Morando.

While best known as the drummer for Liily (and for the Regrettes, from 2015 to 2018), Morando also plays guitar. Additionally, he has also collaborated with Cyrus on several of her albums, including her most recent release, Bass Persuades. For the project, he co-produced the album’s title track alongside Cyrus, as well as several others, including “Aftermath” and “REDLIGHTS.” The musician also has songwriting credits, co-writing “Innocent Ways” with Cyrus and being credited on “Aftermath.”

Morando also produced two songs, “Handstand” and “Violet Chemistry,” from the singer’s Endless Summer Vacation LP.

He also collaborated with Cyrus on her 2025 album, Something Beautiful, contributing as both a producer and songwriter on several tracks. Morando also played drums on the record and made a cameo in the “End of the World” music video.

The drummer, born in 1998, is six years Cyrus’s junior. (His birthday also happens to fall exactly a week ahead of the singer’s, on November 16.)

Cyrus opened up about their slight age gap in a 2024 interview with Harper’s Bazaar: “He grew up with a laptop. I had a desktop computer that I shared with my brothers and sisters. … Honestly, he’s raised our dog off Reddit. I’m like, Are you sure we’re supposed to be doing this? And he’s like, On Reddit it says blah, blah, blah.”

Along with his musical endeavors, the drummer has dabbled in fashion design too, with Cyrus as his muse.

Cyrus revealed in September 2021 that Morando contributed cartoon designs to a custom vegan leather set by designer Shane Kastl, which Cyrus wore for a performance that month.

“This look is a one-of-a-kind collaboration between two of my favorite emerging artists, Maxx Morando and Shane Kastl,” Cyrus said of the special look in an interview. “Their collaboration is the perfect example of sustainability becoming the next fashion phase, and it proves that anything can be reinvented, which resonates with me deeply.”

In an interview for Bazaar’s December 2024 cover story, Cyrus opened up about her relationship with Morando, saying, “He’s very similar to me. We just don’t take life too seriously.”

She also shared how working with Morando on musical projects helped them bond: “I worked with my dad forever. That’s how me and my ex-husband met each other. I’ve always worked with the people that I love,” Cyrus says. “And Maxx just inspires me so much.”

The couple’s engagement was confirmed in December 2025, after Cyrus sparked rumors by wearing a diamond sparkler on her left-hand ring finger at the premiere of Avatar: Fire and Ash in LA.

Morando keeps an extremely private, low profile in both his personal and professional life. While the musician does have an Instagram, he rarely posts, aside from sharing new music that he works on with both his band and Cyrus.

In March 2023, a source told People that Morando is a “cool guy” who is drama-free, a trait that Cyrus finds extremely attractive.

“He has no interest in being a huge celebrity; he’s very low-key. Miley loves these qualities,” the source said. “Miley can be herself. They are supportive of each other’s careers. Miley is enjoying life and things are great.”

Following a year-long engagement, the Morando and Cyrus officially wed in an intimate ceremony held in Palm Springs, California. The couple shared photos from the wedding on Instagram, which included black-and-white portraits of the couple with their dog, as well as a sweet photo of them kissing after saying “I do.”

For the ceremony, the bride wore a long-sleeve, backless Saint Laurent wedding gown, while Morando kept things classic in a black suit.

The poolside ceremony took place at Frank Sinatra’s former home, which was transformed with hundreds of white roses for the occasion. In photos obtained by DeuxMoi, the couple could be seen exchanging vows by the pool, in front of an intimate crowd of guests dressed in all-black attire.

#6632. Chicken Francese

Chicken Francese is a staple at your favorite Italian restaurants. But sometimes, you don't want to empty your wallet for this classic dinner favorite. That's where I come in! Francese is a preparation (much like Milanese) that can be used with all types of meat and seafood, from shrimp to veal. For chicken, it involves dredging cutlets in flour and beaten egg, creating a pseudo-batter. The cutlets are then pan-fried and made crispy, albeit temporarily. See, chicken Francese is one of those dishes that epitomizes "crispy gone soggy"—a texture sensation that is one of my absolute favorites. In this case, the chicken becomes "soggy" because you finish them by simmering it in a rich, lemony sauce that will knock your socks off.

It might seem strange, but it’s such an iconic flavor/texture combination. Also, it is very easy to make and comes together in under an hour. What could be better?!

Place 1 chicken breast on a cutting board. Using a sharp chef’s knife held parallel to the cutting board, slice into the thickest side of the breast, cutting three-quarters of the way through. Fold the top piece back (as if you were opening a book) and continue to cut until the breast is divided into 2 thinner cutlets. Repeat with the remaining chicken breast for a total of 4 cutlets. Working one piece at a time, place each cutlet between 2 sheets of plastic wrap. Using a meat mallet or the bottom of a small heavy skillet, pound the chicken to about 1/4" thick. Season all over with salt and pepper.

In a shallow dish, beat eggs, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt. Pour 1/2 cup flour into another shallow dish.

In a large, heavy skillet over medium heat, heat oil. Working in batches, coat cutlets in flour, shaking off excess, then dip into the egg mixture, turning to coat.

Place cutlets in the oil, being careful not to overcrowd the skillet, and cook, turning halfway through, until golden brown, 5 to 7 minutes.

Transfer cutlets to a paper towel-lined plate to drain and season with salt and pepper.

Wipe out the skillet, then heat over medium heat. Add five Tbsp. butter and the remaining one Tbsp. flour, stirring until just beginning to foam and the butter is melted, 3 to 5 minutes. Whisk in wine. Increase heat to medium-high and bring to a boil. Cook, stirring, until slightly reduced, 1 to 2 minutes. Add stock, lemon zest, and lemon juice and return to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and cook, whisking constantly, until the sauce is reduced by about one-third, 3 to 5 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add lemon slices and remaining 1 Tbsp. butter and cook, stirring, until the sauce is glossy, 2 to 3 minutes more.

Return chicken to the sauce and cook, turning halfway through, until heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.

Transfer chicken to a platter and pour the sauce over. Top with lemon slices and parsley.

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

If you have any leftovers, store them in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Luckily, this dish is used to being a tad soggy and lends itself well to being reheated in the microwave.

For her Icons interview with Harper’s Bazaar this past July, she opened up about her style, saying: “I’m a different person than I was 10 years ago, obviously, but I’ve always loved a leather jacket and a leather pair of pants or some jeans.” Clearly, that’s not going to change with impending motherhood.

On this outing, Gabbriette kept it understated, pairing her simple black dress with a set of leather ballet flats, a chunky bracelet, and a quilted top-handle tote bag from Chanel. Healy, meanwhile, wore a gray tee and distressed jeans with gray boots and a navy zip-up jacket.

#6630. How Am I Supposed to Survive the Apocalypse Without My Phone?

Anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones. Last week’s tech outages––first, a failure of Microsoft’s systems, then, a national grounding of flights, followed by problems from Charles Schwab to Apple iCloud––were a reminder of how fragile our digital infrastructure is, especially at the dawn of AI. Preppers on Reddit, better known for discussing generators and the storage of food, began talking about how to AI–apocalypse proof the devices we’re all so dependent on. “getting serious about my preps with all the cyber attacks going on,” one user wrote. “I work for a security company so I get a front row seat to a lot of the chaos. I’m specifically prepping for prolonged loss of power.”

Many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations. “I had huge, huge spikes in traffic,” said Jackson Studner, creator of Nomad and a student at Millersville University of Pennsylvania. (“I’m not a company or a startup, just a college student who enjoys building useful things and sharing them,” Studner’s website reads.) With the help of his professors, he built Nomad to provide some entertainment on camping trips and cross-country trips with friends. They’d hit a dead zone, and realize they wanted to watch a movie, or run video game software. Nomad is a miniscule server with TV and films, the entire Wikipedia library, and portable Wi-Fi, and offline maps. “I really like the reliability aspect,” Studner tells me. “I like to own my stuff. It's kind of that simple.” He’s also added navigation for his new community preparing for the apocalypse (or at least a grid shutdown). “It will actually tell you how to go along the road, it can tell you how to walk there, it'll calculate times, that kind of stuff,” he said.

Elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber. Sherwood is best known for posting explainer videos showing viewers how to build their “homelabs”—personal, at-home computing devices—under the name Crosstalk Solutions.

The interest in Project Nomad, Sherwood said, has been overwhelming. “It’s got over 40,000 stars on GitHub, which means that 40,000 people not only saw the project and were on the page, but they clicked the little button to favorite it. And I'm getting over 200,000 views on the website per month,” he said.

Despite his new fans, Sherwood himself isn’t a prepper. He was inspired by the Information Technology Disaster Resource Center (ITDRC), a non-profit that goes into disasters and provides internet services when they are completely down. “I had the opportunity to go on deployment with [ITDRC] when Hurricane Ian came through, and I saw firsthand all these people that were offline. It was a disaster. Getting people back online was almost as important as the food and water supplies that were getting set up to help with the recovery,” he explained.

Studner wasn’t a prepper either–– at first. But since Nomad took off and he’s found himself in more “prepper” corners of the internet, his feelings have slightly changed. “It’s for peace of mind. I have my little go bag. I'm not too, too worried about it, but I like to know that if there ever was a real problem, I'd be okay in that situation.”

#6629. Glove Shoes Are Having a Major Fashion Moment

The ultra-soft style is showing up everywhere, from ballet flats to polished heels and boots.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Glove shoes are certainly having a moment. Made from soft, pliable leather that molds to the foot, they often feature a higher vamp than traditional shoes and come in everything from flats to heels and boots. The style showed up across both the fall and spring runways, with high fashion designers giving it plenty of attention. Naturally, that makes us pay attention to it, too. Ahead, dive into the trend and shop it for yourself.

Surely you’ve heard of the jazz shoe trend by now, right? Some such styles are glove-like, but you can also find an abundance of “regular” ballet flats in a glove style. Personally, I can’t stop wearing the pair I have from Steve Madden.

If you really want to be the most fashion-forward person in your office (without looking like a clown), wear a pair of glove heels to your next board meeting. It’s a subtle swap that fashion insiders will immediately recognize. My personal favorites are from Bottega Veneta and 3.1 Phillip Lim.

Proenza Schouler Glove 70MM Leather Pumps

Now, when it comes to glove boots, your options are a bit more limited. That said, if any of these pairs speak to you, I recommend jumping on the chance to make them yours. Whether you go for a flat or heeled rendition, these are a sleek alternative to your average winter boot.

#6628. Vogue’s Best Dressed People of 2026

Our goal was 50—just 50!—of the best-dressed people of the year, a list to commemorate the unforgettable fashion moments of a very topsy-turvy 2026. Sounds easy…but, well, list-making never is. There were athletes who turned game days into runways, actors who owned the red carpet and the sidewalk, and method-dressing movie stars who artfully ignored the meaning of the word cut.

We wanted them all, plus some highly fashionable characters from unexpected fields and walks of life, and we wanted couples, which we insisted should be counted as singletons (a technicality!). We struggled and horse-traded and voted and arrived finally at…55! (The same number as last year.) Here is the fruit of our labor: an unranked, diligently categorized, highly subjective list of Vogue’s best dressed of 2026. And it all begins with our cover star, a selection that was the result of a rather heated debate. Enjoy!

Written by: Christian Allaire, Margaux Anbouba, Taylor Antrim, Max Berlinger, Laird Borrelli-Persson, Anna Cafolla, Liam Hess, Alexandra Hildreth, Hannah Jackson, Joan Kennedy, Irene Kim, Anna Grace Lee, Nicole Phelps, Madeleine Schulz, and Emma Specter.

STORRIE TIME Conner Storrie brings the Ken-ergy in a miniaturized version of his Gucci Best Dressed cover look. Coach watch pendant.

Why 2026 was his year: Playing brooding Russian hockey player Ilya Rozanov in the gay romance Heated Rivalry—in various states of deshabille—launched this 26-year-old Hollywood hopeful waiting tables in Los Angeles to cultural supernova. His last 12 months have seen a kind of fashion miracle: Storrie is now better known for what he wears than what he doesn’t. Click here for his cover-story conversation with Chloe Malle—which ranged from Storrie’s punk roots to his adoration of Parker Posey, his side hustle in “provocateur” photography, and more.

Friends, lovers, collaborators—occasionally all at once.

Why 2026 was their year: Him: Train Daddy in The Gilded Age; Her: Wicked stepmother in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story (and more).

Their couple style, in essence: Hudson Valley cabincore meets Tom Ford heat.

Kravitz wears The Row. Styles wears The Row and Adidas.

Their year in fashion: Excellent outerwear, statement headgear, rave-ready sunglasses, plenty of The Row.

Their couple style, in essence: Kiss all the time. Dress alike, more than occasionally.

From left: Imhof wears Balenciaga, Teuscher wears Rodarte; both wear Valentino.

Why 2026 was their year: Teuscher traded Lincoln Center for Hong Kong to star in her partner Imhof’s queer, Shakespearean House of Swans.

Their couple style, in essence: Berghain Romeo and Juliet.

Why 2026 was their year: Barone released comedy special Galaxy Brain; Skinner got to work on Overcompensating season 2. Together: their riotous podcast, Ride, and Halloween domination.

Their couple style, in essence: Newport Beach heartthrobs, if they canvassed for Zohran.

Left: Both in Dior. Right: Arquette wears Circus of Magdela; Lean wears Giorgio Armani.

Why 2026 was their year: Lean bringing down the house at the VMAs, while writing duets with Arquette; the couple hard-launching at Dior Men’s spring 2027 show.

Their couple style, in essence: Shades of blue (or bleu).

Left: Rosalía in Stella McCartney. Right: Bahia wears Saint Laurent; Rosalía wears Vivienne Westwood.

Their year in fashion: Contrasting-yet-coordinated masc-for-femme dressing, conjuring early days Justin and Hailey.

Why we can’t get enough: Two words: tooth necklace.

He said; she said: MGK to Vogue: “I started kind of respecting my upkeep, and I’ve watched things open up.” Johnson to Vogue: “[Musicians] like me, I don’t know what to say.”

Their couple style, in essence: Hoodies, diamonds, beanies, grommets, lace, leather, fangs. Misery business.

LIFE IN PLASTIC, IT’S FANTASTIC! Master of the step-and-repeat, Kendall Jenner set the gold standard for polka-dots in her Valentino Academy Gala dress.

The category is: great gowns, beautiful gowns.

Jenner wears Armani; Alexander Calder earrings.

Her year in fashion: Winged Victory at the Met, snagging ultra-rare Calder earrings for her first Lido, spreading the gospel of The Row, and perfecting polka dots at the Academy Gala.

Why we can’t get enough: She wears clothes like it’s her job.

Why 2026 was her year: Rose, Fatherland, and Project Hail Mary! (And, ahem, Digger.)

Highlight reel: Matières Fécales’ riff on the bar suit; Chanel’s riff on the hedgehog.

Her year in fashion: Dior standouts (acid green Poiret punk and impressionistic water lilies, specifically), plus an Issey Miyake breastplate, Marc Jacobs sequins, and Lii color blocking.

Best look of 2026: That star-spangled scarlet High Sport halter dress with a swishy fringed hem for the London premiere of Toy Story 5—a clever, playful wink to the film’s universe that still felt fashion.

Mulligan wears (from left): Colleen Allen; Dries Van Noten; The Row; Celine.

Why 2026 was her year: Lending her voice to Wildwood, scoring an Emmy nom for Beef season 2, getting a CBE from the King (she wore The Row).

Best look: That triptych of pixelated floral brocades from Julian Klausner’s fall 2026 Dries Van Noten collection. Bonus points for the pockets in the top!

Why this was her year: An awards-season run for Hamnet; an ultra-chic stint on the jury at Cannes.

Best look of 2026: Schiaparelli’s spiky “Isabella Blowfish” dress was a creepy-cheeky wow on the runway—and doubly satisfying on the Croisette.

A DOLL’S HOUSE Who says you can only wear your Met Gala dress once? Back in her Barbie Dreamhouse closet, Paloma Elsesser plays dress-up in her bespoke Bureau of Imagination gown.

They’re wearing your favorite brand—you just don’t know it yet.

Elsesser wears (from left): Junya Watanabe; Comme des Garçons, Phoebe Philo shoes, Chanel bag; Goyagoma.

Why 2026 was her year: When she wasn’t on the hunt for her next vintage deep cut? Hitting the runway for Ferragamo and Junya Watanabe and debuting Francesco Risso’s Bureau of Imagination at the Met.

She’ll get bragging rights for: The Bureau of Imagination gown—patchworked, painted, and embellished by “a squadron of people.” A true one-of-a-kind.

Thompson wears Giovanna Flores; Kallmeyer.

Why 2026 was her year: A Golden Globes nomination for Hedda; the runaway thriller His & Hers; and her Broadway debut in Fear of 13 alongside Adrien Brody.

She’ll get bragging rights for: Her support of all things indie is as evident in her work as in her wardrobe: just take the enviably cool Giovanna Flores patchwork dress she wore on a sweltering day in New York.

Peak wears (from left): Lii; Diotima; Torishéju.

Why 2026 was her year: She drummed up Hunger Games hype, toggling her looks between indie darlings and bona fide fashion-girl pulls.

She’ll get bragging rights for wearing: A scrunched-up black top and red cut-out leather skirt from London-based Torishéju; the standout textured Diotima dress from this season; and New York favorite Liii.

She’ll get bragging rights for wearing: A custom dress from Polimoda fashion school graduate Elias Matso, made entirely from steel boning and beads in a process that took over 300 hours.

Her year in fashion: Ditching goth—at least until Wednesday season 3.

OUT OF THE BOX On the lively streets of New York City, Sarah Pidgeon does her best CBK in a leopard-print Adam Lippes coat. Susan Alexandra pigeon charm.

Why 2026 was her year: She introduced a new generation to Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy—and her Yohji Yamamoto-filled closet—in Love Story.

Give her an Oscar for this look: The lacy aqua blue slip dress she wore to the Chanel Pre-Oscars party married CBK-ish ’90s minimalism with present-day Blazy-mania.

Why 2026 was her year: The Drama! Spider-Man! The Odyssey! Dune! Oh, and she found time to marry Tom Holland, too.

Give her an Oscar for this look: The white strapless Matières Fécales gown with matching feathered wings while promoting The Odyssey was pure Athena realness.

Edgar-Jones wears (from left): Miu Miu; Andreas Kronthaler for Vivienne Westwood; Rodarte.

Why 2026 was her year: The 18th-century-inspired Sense and Sensibility press tour, featuring a dreamy blush Galliano jacket worn with jeans; sexed-up pantaloon sets from Dries Van Noten and Colleen Allen; and lots and lots of Stella McCartney-era Chloé.

Up next: Going toe-to-toe with Michelle Williams in A Place in Hell and bringing another book club favorite to the big screen in Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow.

Robbie wears Schiaparelli; Dilara Findikoglu.

Why we can’t get enough: Schiaparelli couture with Elizabeth Taylor’s legendary Taj Mahal diamonds one day, cutoff jorts the next.

Up Next: How will she method-dress for Untitled Ocean’s Eleven Prequel?

Fanning wears (from left): Robert Wun; Givenchy by Sarah Burton; Evan Clayton.

Why 2026 was her year: Earned her first Oscar nomination for Sentimental Value, delivered Margot’s Got Money Troubles, and dressed in her Capitol best for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Her style, in essence: Anything can be a hat!

OFF THE SHELF Olivia Rodrigo, here in vintage Rudi Gernreich, brought major flower power with her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival. Susan Alexandra flower and mushroom charms.

Pop stars or politicians—they’re all headliners to us.

Why 2026 was her year: It was a legacy-defining one between Rodrigo’s best album yet (hello, seven Grammy nominations) and her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields music festival, which raised $20 million to support nonprofits for women and girls.

Her year in fashion: She joined a long line of badasses who’ve subverted the babydoll dress—Kathleen Hanna and Courtney Love come to mind.

Why we can’t get enough: From this summer’s ribbon-cutting at the Barack Obama Presidential Center in Thom Browne to attending the U.S. Open in red, white, and blue Chanel, she makes patriotism look chic.

The look that deserved a push notification: The Acne Studios skirt custom-printed with a photo of her late mother Marian Robinson, a gesture that brought the former president—and the rest of us—to tears.

Dion wears (from left): Tom Ford; Dior; Chanel; Chanel.

Why 2026 was their year: A triumphant return to the stage following her stiff person syndrome diagnosis meant 16 sold-out shows at Paris’s Plénitude Arena, plus daily pap walks outside of Le Royal Monceau.

The look that deserved a push notification: The custom Chanel sweetheart-neckline gown that took 1,380 hours to make—a recreation of her 1997 Oscars dress. Our hearts will go on!

Why 2026 was her year: Wrestling with mortality on Lost Weekend; stealing scenes in Primetime.

The look that deserved a push notification: In Venice, a lesson in indie-darling dressing: Gucci skirt suit, below-the-knee tattoo, visible leg hair.

Why 2026 was her year: The Minnesota senator-to-be’s midterm victory made her the first-ever Indigenous woman elected to the United States Senate.

The look that deserved a push notification: Victory called for a sleek burgundy suit and a traditional pair of dentalium shell earrings by Yurok artist Jessica Mendez.

TINY FURNITURE Just like Mary, Cole Escola is the picture-perfect homemaker in the Christopher John Rogers jumpsuit they wore to the Tonys. Movado watch. Jennifer Behr earrings.

Imitation may be the sincerest form of flattery, but there’s no replicating one-of-one style.

Escola wears (from left): Chanel; Eckhaus Latta; vintage Eve Stillman.

Why 2026 was their year: Oh, Mary! went on the road, and Escola’s Miss Piggy became the in-the-works screenplay we didn’t know we needed.

Highlight reel: Coco cosplay at Chanel couture; an “ibuprofen”-pink Christopher John Rogers jumpsuit at the Tonys; an Eckhaus Latta deep cut at the CFDA Awards.

Why 2026 was her year: Who else could collect their Golden Globe in a bejeweled Schiaparelli whale tail?

Her best look: The trompe l’oeil Thom Browne at the SAG Awards, with her daughter Rue Rose on hand to adjust her train. As Taylor put it: “A very expensive stylist.”

Why 2026 was his year: A longtime Comme des Garçons acolyte, Sedaris promoted his latest book, The Land and Its People, in layers of deconstructed tailoring, voluminous skirts, and oddball shoes.

Why we can’t get enough: Dressed in a diaphanous layered ensemble for Late Night With Seth Meyers, he quipped, “I think of this as a sports skirt.”

Ellis Ross wears (from left): Prada; Balenciaga; Dries Van Noten.

Why this was her year: A Broadway debut in Every Brilliant Thing, an expanding Pattern Beauty lineup, a daytime Emmy for her show, Solo Traveling—and she found time to start styling herself.

Best look of 2026: That marigold Balenciaga at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala; beautifully textured, quintessentially her (with a dash of Law Roach).

Why we can’t get enough: What was the American Hagwon author’s first fashion flex when fiction started paying the bills? Early days Thom Browne. “I bought one of Thom’s first sweaters,” Lee told Vogue.

Best look of 2026: Her go-to matching pinstriped Comme des Garçons blazer and dress for large speaking events. Who said a uniform can’t have style?

Hill wears (from left): Bottega Veneta; Saint Laurent; Balenciaga.

Why 2026 was her year: Became a BET Living Legend in voluminous, ruffled Saint Laurent with wrap-around sunglasses; reunited with Wyclef to celebrate the 30th anniversary of The Score; sat front row at Balenciaga spring 2027 as “Ready or Not” blared.

Her style in essence: Can’t take my eyes off you.

PAPER DOLL Audrey Nuna puts a bow on 2026 in the Thom Browne cape she wore to the Golden Globes.

You’ll never again have to ask, “Wait, where do I know them from?”

Where you know her from: If you don’t know her face, odds are you’ve heard her sing: Nuna lent her voice to Mira in the Oscar- and Grammy-winning KPop Demon Hunters.

Best outfit of 2026: The cocoon-like black cape dress embellished with bows from Thom Browne—one of her more understated looks, if you can believe it.

You’ve heard them: Honking on their Getting Killed tour, SNL, or frontman Cameron Winter’s Carnegie Hall live album.

Their year in fashion: Well-worn band tees, threadbare tank tops, bug-eyed sunglasses, and dresses over jeans are par for the course. Their too-cool-for-school style is just that: too cool.

Why you should know her: The singer was marked safe from one-hit-wonderdom with her third album, Blue Island.

Best outfit of 2026: The eccentric, richly embellished Space Age Rabanne dress she wore to the Grammys was totally out of this world.

Where you know her from: Apple TV’s Shrinking and Kane Parsons’s instant horror classic Backrooms.

Best outfit of 2026: The peachy fall 2011 Prada minidress with rounded sleeves, sharp front pleats, and a belted drop waist that she wore during the Toronto International Film Festival. If Miuccia hasn’t already come calling…she should.

Why you should know her: The actor—and niece of fashion designer Anna Sui—proved good taste is genetic while making the rounds for I Want Your Sex and The Studio.

Best outfit of 2026: At Sundance, she plumbed the family archives, settling on a funky, faux fur-trimmed slip dress and matching bonnet. She got it from her auntie!

Great on the red carpet; even better on a morning-after coffee run.

Lawrence wears (from left): Dior jacket, Completedworks earrings; The Row polo, Siedrés pants, Tory Burch necklace, The Row loafers; Junk Food T-shirt, Dries Van Noten skirt, Ancient Greek slippers, Hermès bag.

Her year in fashion: Vintage graphic tees; flowing trousers; boho scarves; slip-on Vans; oversized sunglasses; pendant necklaces; statement bags of the highest order.

Her style, in essence: Skate park chaperone.

Jacobson wears (from left): Khaite; Dilara Findikoglu; Mel Usine; Conner Ives.

Why we can’t get enough: The theatricality we want from a Yale Drama grad: high collars, slashed abs, daring necklines, sleek layering.

On the clock: Her 2026 Met Gala look—as a Joan of Arc-esque figure in a coin-and-pin-adorned armored bodysuit by Dilara Findikoglu. Biopic when?

Edebiri wears (from left): Conner Ives; Giovanna Flores; vintage tee, Still Kelly pants, Chanel bag.

Why this was her year: Post-Bear, trying new things with her career (Broadway; Woolf), and her fashion (Giovanna Flores patchwork dress; Chanel tail feathers).

Best look of 2026: She showed the boys how it’s done in a slick Conner Ives suit.

Schafer wears (from left): Prada; Gimaguas dress; Celine.

Best off-duty look of 2026: The silky purple backward button-up over a tomato-red Gimaguas minidress she wore down the Chateau Marmont driveway.

Her style, in essence: Up for anything, from Gustav Klimt’s Mäda Primavesi to dystopian fembot.

Abrams wears (from left): Balenciaga by Nicolas Ghesquière top, Hamish Olrik pants, Chanel shoes; Colleen Allen; vintage tee from Moth Food, Chanel pants, shoes, and bag.

Best off-duty look of 2026: The sporty, vintage-looking “Vote” baseball tee paired with high-waisted wool trousers and Chanel’s signature cap-toe shoes: effortless, elegant, utterly cool.

Her style, in essence: West LA girl on London sabbatical.

MVPs and benchwarmers alike stole the show with their ’fits this year.

Osaka wears Miss Claire Sullivan; Hana Yagi.

Why 2026 was her year: The four-time Grand Slam champ reached her first-ever Wimbledon quarterfinal and went all-in on her fashion, on and off the court.

Her slam-dunk look: Acing Wimbledon whites in a Hana Yagi walkout look inspired by traditional Japanese ceremonial attire.

Clarkson wears (from left): Abercrombie & Fitch; vintage T-shirt, Louis Vuitton scarf, Hat Club hat; Chrome Hearts jacket, Saint Laurent pants.

His slam-dunk look: A fitted black Rick Owens long-sleeve and pants amidst the Paris heatwave. He ditched the shirt post-show—not that we’re complaining.

Why 2026 was his year: A ruptured Achilles and dashed World Cup dreams didn’t keep the French footballer from Wimbledon or the Balenciaga front row.

His slam-dunk look: A Miu Miu Canadian tuxedo, vested for maximum bicep-baring.

They are not like other guys, in that you’ll never catch them in a snoozy black tux.

O’Connor wears (from left): Lemaire; vintage jacket, Adidas track pants; Hermès.

Best look of 2026: The all-black Hermès leather shirt-and-trousers ensemble that gagged the internet.

Why we can’t get enough: The swerve from tweedy London boy to louche fashion lad. We always knew he had it in him.

Why this was his year: Euphoria, Disclosure Day, and Michael (plus an Emmy nomination for The Four Seasons); shutting down every single step-and-repeat along the way.

Best outfit of 2026: The custom purple caped Valentino look dotted with Boucheron jewels was the antidote to the standard-issue suit.

Innanen wears (from left): a vintage tee, Jeanerica jeans, Loewe bag; 6397 shirt and pants, Sena loafers, Aaron Levine bag; vintage tee, Jeanerica jeans, Dunst jacket.

Why 2026 was his year: From season 2 of Adults to the front rows of Paris Fashion Week, Innanen reminded us that he is far more than just a TikTok star.

Why we can’t get enough: On one New York City scorcher, he made it clear he was in heat in a Horny graphic tee.

Malkovich wears (from left): Dior; Chanel; Aubero.

Why 2026 was his year: Malkovich has always been a bona fide fashion obsessive (lest we forget his past ventures in menswear design as “Technobohemian”). Wild Horse Nine gave him the red carpets to prove it.

Breakout moment of 2026: The Dior suit with a ruff collar he wore at the Venice Film Festival was a cross between a Tudor courtier and frill-necked lizard.

They’re your favorite fashion editor’s favorite fashion editor…and stylist and buyer and model.

On Marci: JW Anderson shirt, Ruadh jeans, Loewe bag. On Lori: Nahmias shirt, Chanel skirt, Alaïa bag.

Why the fashion industry loves them: No one inspires envy as consistently as aunt-niece duo Lori and Marci Hirshleifer, who operate the dynastic Manhasset store Hirshleifers.

Why 2026 was their year: At a time when everyone is looking to amp up their personal style, these two have it in spades.

Bellizzi wears (from left): Dior by John Galliano; Chanel; Versace.

Why 2026 was her year: After receiving an Oscar nomination for her work on Marty Supreme, Bellizzi styled her first Vogue shoot and pulled double duty at 6397’s spring 2027 show, both styling and walking in it.

Highlight reel: Galliano Dior, Blazy Chanel, Dario Versace.

Why 2026 was her year: When she isn’t styling Vogue Italia shoots or walking the Conner Ives runway, Lebasi consults for CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist Miss Claire Sullivan.

Best outfit: At the 2026 CFDA Fashion Fund Finalist cocktail, Lebasi elevated a white tee and blue jeans with a Miss Claire Sullivan bolero. Someone’s already got the 2027 Met Gala theme down.

Left: Rick Owens jacket, Afghani embroidered chapan, Sea trousers, Kero shoes, COS cummerbund, Chimi sunglasses. Right: Miu Miu pants and shoes, Prada button-up, Calvin Klein bra, Gentle Monster sunglasses.

Why this was her year: At the spring 2027 collections, the Swedish-Pakistani catwalker seemed to open (Fendi, Victoria Beckham, Sacai) or close (Tom Ford, Hermès, Louis Vuitton) every show that mattered.

Her best look: The teeny tank top and hip-slung jeans she was spotted wearing off-runway at Paris Fashion Week would get a nod of approval from Haider Ackermann, who put her in the season’s most barely-there bathing suit at Tom Ford.

Left: Ojuromi. Center: Ojuromi wears a dress by Debby Fasingha. Right: Fasingha.

Why the fashion industry loves them: This duo grew their homespun, high-energy Lagos fashion showcases into a global sensation. Through Ojuromi and Fasingha’s lens, fashion feels fresh, personal, and full of possibility.

Why 2026 was their year: After a video of Ojuromi walking in Fasingha’s DIY, Chanel-inspired looks went viral, the model made her runway debut at the brand’s spring 2027 show.

#6626. The Best Foods To Buy At Costco In November

Our editors were blown away by one game-changing snack.

The holiday season is on the horizon, and Costco is celebrating with plenty of festive foods in every corner of the warehouse. Aside from the obligatory pumpkin pie, you can find party-approved appetizers, cozy bakery treats, and plenty of fall-forward snacks.

I spend all year keeping tabs on the latest and greatest products to hit Costco shelves. And as someone who writes about Costco for a living, I have a hot take: The food at the warehouse right now is the best it’s been all year.

Here’s what’s available this November—there are some treats you don’t want to miss.

The viral sensation has officially hit Costco. The Dot Cakes is a bakery on Long Island, New York, that exploded in popularity this summer thanks to its signature dessert: a single-serving cake in a cup covered in a generous layer of nonpareil sprinkles. Now, instead of waiting in long lines or trying to recreate it at home, Costco members can buy a six-pack of the real thing.

Each box includes both chocolate and vanilla cake, and both flavors are perfectly nostalgic. They taste like the best-ever birthday cake from your childhood, and the crunch of the sprinkles makes the experience even more fun.

It admittedly takes a lot for us to get excited about grapes—but these are worth the hype. Shine Muscat is a premium variety from Japan, famous for its large, sweet, seedless fruit. Many of the ones sold in the U.S. are imported from East Asia, including these Korean grapes now available at Costco.

I’ve had the pleasure of trying the grapes in smoothie form at a Costco food court in Seoul, but the real thing is even better. Our editors couldn’t stop eating them and compared the flavor to a plum or lychee. And at $10.99, they’re a fun upgrade that costs only a bit more than standard table grapes.

Want takeout flavors without takeout prices? Costco is now selling a noodle stir-fry kit that can feed the whole family for around $15. Each tray includes crispy breaded chicken pieces, yakisoba noodles, vegetables, and a sweet-and-savory sauce.

The meal is super easy to put together: Just crisp up the chicken in the oven or air fryer, then heat everything else in a pan. Costco is generous with the chicken and noodles, so the kit can provide at least four substantial servings. But if you need just one reason to add it to your cart, do it for the sauce. It’s just sweet enough with the slightest hint of spice.

Cabot Creamery has already combined its cheddar with popcorn, but this fall-forward version balances the sharp, salty flavor with a bit of sweetness. Each bag includes two types of popcorn: one seasoned with Cabot’s famous Seriously Sharp Cheddar and another with a maple syrup-flavored coating. Both are delicious on their own, but together? Magic happens.

The salty-sweet combo really works here, reminding us of those large popcorn tins with three different compartments, except everything’s mixed together. Your holiday movie marathon needs a bag of this.

Fans of the Kirkland Signature peanut butter pretzels need to grab this sweet treat. Jif’s Snappers combine mini pretzels, the brand’s creamy peanut butter, and a drizzle of milk chocolate. We love that there’s a higher peanut butter-to-pretzel ratio than with Kirkland Signature's version (and the PB is much softer). This snack has everything: It’s salty, sweet, crunchy, creamy, and impossible to put down.

Step aside, Snap, Crackle, and Pop. The brand Cloud 9 has upgraded the cereal-based sweet with flavors inspired by mango sticky rice. Each bar combines puffed rice with dried mango, coconut milk, and shredded coconut. And the Delish team agrees: This is arguably the best snack Costco has sold all year. It’s loaded with mango, lightly sweet, and full of interesting textures. Buy a bag and thank us later.

In just a few years, Swedish candy went from an uncommon novelty to a permanent fixture in the candy aisle. Now, Costco carries a Rolling Pin variety pack that includes sour gummies and foam candy (a Swedish staple with a marshmallow-like texture).

This 30-ounce bag features a wide variety of chewy textures and fruity flavors. If you’re just now dipping your toes into the world of Swedish candy, this is a great (and affordable) way to start.

Need fall breakfast inspo? Look no further. The newest addition to the Costco bakery is this maple pecan coffee cake, which is loaded with cream cheese, pecans, and maple flavor. The cake is topped with a crumbly pecan butter streusel and drizzled with the same icing Costco uses on its danishes.

Each coffee cake is $15, but it’s arguably worth much more given its sheer size. This thing is a behemoth—it’s tall and absolutely loaded with toppings. There’s also a thick layer of filling in the center that tastes nearly identical to pecan pie filling.

Baked brie is a party showstopper, and Costco now carries a kit with everything you need in one convenient package. Stonemill Kitchens’ kit includes puff pastry, a wheel of brie, chopped pecans, and caramel apple cranberry chutney. You’ll need to assemble it yourself before you throw it in the oven, but the instructions couldn’t be simpler. The puff pastry even comes with a sheet of parchment paper to protect your baking sheet!

And the results are straight-up showstopping. The melty, creamy brie pairs perfectly with the pastry and toppings. The chutney, despite the caramel in the name, isn’t too sweet—it adds just the right amount of festive holiday flavor. It’s so good that News and Features Editor Amanda Mactas even did a happy dance after taking a bite.

#6625. Louis Vuitton Takes Its Place at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix Finish Line

A handcrafted trunk awaited the winner, Max Verstappen.

When Max Verstappen crossed the finish line at the Las Vegas Formula 1 Grand Prix on Saturday night, after a gripping race that saw the championship driver battle to maintain the tightest of leads against rivals George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, his trophy came in very special packaging: a bespoke Louis Vuitton trunk. For the past two seasons, Trophy Trunks have been presented to the winner of the annual Las Vegas event, which sees drivers race on a thrilling course that winds along the famous Strip. They have also been presented to the winners of the World Cup, America’s Cup, and the NBA Finals. Louis Vuitton had a strong presence across the whole race weekend, hosting a suite where guests including Teyana Taylor watched the events from above the track and were able to get an early look at the trunk.

The Las Vegas trunk was, like all Louis Vuitton custom pieces, made at Asnières-sur-Seine, a commune in northern France. It was handcrafted by 25 artisans, made to the specific dimensions of the trophy. The Trophy Trunks are a remarkable mingling of the old and the new. They use the traditional craftsmanship techniques that have defined the house for over 170 years. All construction of the trunks’ wood, leather, and locks was done with the same techniques LV has used since the beginning, meaning that in many ways the Trophy Trunks differ little from its trunks from a century ago. The modern energy of motor racing comes through via subtle touches like the two stripes across the trunk that make a large V, a nod to both Vuitton and victory—they’re black-and-white checkered as a nod to the Formula 1 finish line. A small badge that calls back to the early days of trunk travel and bears the winning driver’s initials was added this year.

Louis Vuitton’s relationship with Formula 1 began with the Grand Prix de Monaco, which the brand began creating Trophy Trunks for in 2021. In 2025, it became an official partner of the league, and this year, LV created trunks for all 24 of the season’s races. In early December, the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix will mark the final 2026 race.

#6624. Best Men's Studded Belts 2026: From RRL to Our Legacy

Most people might build an outfit around a pair of shoes. Others, around a jacket. But few, surprisingly, do it around a belt.

At GQ, we’ve always said that the overlooked belt is more than the sum of its buckle and holes. Not only will it stop your slacks from going south, but a good leather belt can make just as much of a statement as your shoes, and deliver as much of a stylistic flourish as a tie. Unconvinced? Enter: The studded belt. (Which, coincidentally, we're now increasingly seeing be offered by some of the most imitated brands in the industry, from Lemaire to RRL, Mfpen to Our Legacy.)

The charm of the studded belt is that it’s a vibe chameleon. Its decorative elements can pay tribute to any number of aesthetics, from Americana to punk to European artistry. And while any one will easily provide further flair to an already-singing outfit, the best ones also single-handedly bring even the most minimalist wardrobe to life. (And to be honest, that’s how I feel studded belts are best worn today: Against a white tee and jeans, for an easy win without changing your whole look.)

To help you find the right one for you, I've sorted through the vast waist-wear market to find a selection that won't just make your outfits sing, but set them on course for superstardom. See you out there, Stud.

Let's start gently: Somehow, Anderson’s has made a studded belt that whispers. It’s a small but mighty addition to their lovingly handcrafted Italian leather goods.

“If a stud falls out, make a wish,” is the outlook over at Htc Los Angeles—and they provide plenty of it. A true purveyor of the style, the brand has been specializing in rock-and-roll embellished leather goods since the ’90s. And they aren’t stingy with it either.

Trust Corridor NYC to come in clutch for all of your folksy Americana needs. The worn-in look of their studded belt—made in full-grain leather and tarnished hardware—carries all the tales of someone who’s worn it through the arid badlands.

If the fits over at the Ralph Lauren PoloFest in Tokyo last month have inspired you to join the RL tribe, any one of the many studded belts from RRL (Ralph's ranch-minded line) is a strong place to start.

As you’ll see from our list, Our Legacy—a staple for any serious fashion guy—has secured two call-outs. Here, they cut diamond studs to form a snakeskin-like pattern that, when worn against your best corduroy pants, gives the look some severe shine.

While we’re talking about studded belts as an easy hardware win, they're also the perfect place to score some color points too. Here, the green and orange mixes it up more than traditional turquoise.

Since its founding in 2012, Maximum Henry has been handmaking our favorite leather goods right here in New York City, including their beloved oval buckle belt. But they also know how to do a good, uncomplicated studded belt.

The floral studs on this OL belt aren’t merely decorative, but are punched into the very function of the eyelets. It’s a sweet look, really, and one done so effortlessly.

Dressing for winter, when all you ever want to feel is cozy, can leave you feeling like a schlub. There is, however, an easy fix in the form of the enviably Parisian stylings of Lemaire, who’ve released a brown belt with almond-shaped studs. Wear it with your all-denim outfit or heavy grey wool pants, it’ll make you feel like one of the brand’s cityslicking models in their closely-studied runway shows.

While we’ve so far been paying attention to how studs can add some play, texture still plays a key role to make an outfit sing. A Kind of Guise made their turquoise studded belt with a tan nubuck leather.

Lemaire might be better known for their artsy fabrics and drape-y cuts, but their accessories department is a treasure trove too.

Florals can be a lot generally for most guys, but Mfpen uses theirs sparingly on their lean 2cm wide belt. Made in patent brown leather, it also adds a nice formal sheen to a dark winter ensemble.

We’ve so far seen how studded belts can sway from Americana to minimalist vibes, but we can’t leave out the heavy metal rockers. Heliot Emil shaves off the edges for something more digestible, but still packs enough punch to cut through a monochromatic outfit.

Finally, we've talked a lot about how to add spice to your fit, but what does that mean—really? Eraldo has some answers.

#6622. 2026 Was the Year of the Fashion Bride

If—for a certain set of cool, young designers—doing bridal was once thought uncool, 2026 may have been the year that finally put that notion to rest.

We’ve been seeing the shift for years now: For many brides, the wedding-day dream has gone beyond the beautiful, white, traditionally “bridal” wedding dress. Increasingly, brides want something, well, cool—an expression of their personal brand and sensibility, whether that means a painstakingly sourced archival look or a custom piece by an unexpected designer. This year, that trend was on full display, as wedding fashion increasingly became a stage and cultural touchpoint for brides and designers alike.

2026 was a banner year for high-profile weddings and celebrity brides wearing everything from romantic gowns to razor-sharp suits: Zendaya and Tom Holland, Dua Lipa and Callum Turner, Dove Cameron and Damiano David, Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez, Emma Roberts and Cody John, Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods, to name just a few.

And that’s without even mentioning the “royal wedding” of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce. While the photos are yet to be released (and if you ask Swift bestie Dakota Johnson, they never will be), we do know that Swift became Jonathan Anderson’s first celebrity bride, a move that had people feverishly searching for clues at his Dior Haute Couture show in July. Could it be that white chiffon and degradé lace final gown, which later graced the runway at Vogue World: Milan? Nothing was revealed, apart from Anderson telling Women’s Wear Daily, “It was a joy to work with her. We became very good friends,” and “It’s an emotional thing doing someone’s wedding.”

Dua Lipa’s August wedding, meanwhile, was a fashion extravaganza, starting with a custom Schiaparelli white skirt suit, designed by creative director Daniel Roseberry. Who can forget the image of the pop star, beaming under a burst of confetti as she walked out of the town hall as a newlywed? Her suit was inspired by Bianca Jagger’s bridal look for her wedding to Mick Jagger in Saint-Tropez on May 12, 1971, perhaps the ultimate cool-girl bridal nod. Lipa rounded out her bridal looks with a white leather Bottega Veneta custom gown by Louise Trotter, and a Chanel haute couture gown for her main wedding dress.

Beyond the celeb wedding world, this year saw rising stars and in-demand designers put forward bridal looks, some for the first time. Dilara Findikoglu launched her first bridal capsule, a rule-breaking, lingerie-forward offering adapted from her ready-to-wear line, with campaign photos of models smashing plates, smoking, and mounting their grooms. (“I really believe that the power of my clothes is to bring out the uniqueness in someone,” Findikoglu previously told Vogue. “That’s exactly why they became Dilara Brides: to reveal the most unique version of who they already are.”)

Dilara Findikoglu’s debut bridal collection.

Batsheva debuted her first bridal collection at New York’s Bridal Fashion Week. Christopher John Rogers solidified his status as a sought-after designer for stylish brides, including Vogue fashion market director Naomi Elizée Blue, TikTok brand strategist Ali Lebow, and film director Pam Nasr. In an interview with The New York Times about his rising profile in the wedding world, Rogers even teased his very own bridal collection.

Naomi Elizée Blue in Christopher John Rogers.

CFDA/Vogue Fashion Funders Zoe Gustavia Anna Whalen and Miss Claire Sullivan created custom bridal looks for Architectural Digest senior design editor Hannah Martin and the artist Tourmaline, respectively. Martin’s gown was inspired by a look from Whalen’s spring 2025 collection, featuring a corseted bodice with a padded hip. Whalen previously told Vogue about why she decided to take on a bridal client, a rare move for her. “It aligns so much with my general ethos of garments being these weighted, emotional objects,” Whalen said. “So when it’s the right fit, being able to create that with such intention for somebody else is so beautiful.”

Tourmaline (right) in Miss Claire Sullivan.

Elsewhere, Raul Lopez dressed his friends Juice Rodriguez and Cristal Veras in coordinated Luar for their New York wedding. Gabbriette became the first bride for Matières Fécales, the cult Paris label whose show Rihanna attended in September. And Colleen Allen, winner of the 2026 CFDA Emerging Designer of the Year Award, has quietly become the fashion girls’ dream wedding dress designer, after making a custom look for Charli xcx’s wedding reception last year.

“Bridal” no longer means just one thing. For independent designers, it can be a playground to express something new, a platform for their brand, and, as Joe Bobowicz observed in a Vogue Business article, a dependable revenue stream. And as people expand their ideas of what a wedding can look like—donning colorful gowns in every color from butter yellow to pink to black, and playing with material and silhouette—as we head into 2027, the future of bridal style has never been more thrillingly uncertain.

#6620. Crock-Pot Stuffing

There are only so many dishes you can make in your oven on Thanksgiving, so we’ve made it easy for you with a no-bake stuffing that doesn’t require taking up oven space. Instead, we use a slow cooker that’ll help you whip up your stuffing alongside the stars of the show (roast turkey and pumpkin pie, obviously!). While you buzz around the kitchen, the slow cooker will cook your stuffing for you — resulting in a delicious Thanksgiving side dish waiting for you to serve up.

Arrange a rack in the center of the oven and preheat it to 350°. Spread bread on a baking sheet. Bake the bread, tossing it halfway through, until it is crispy and feels dry. The edges should just be starting to turn golden, which should take about 15 to 20 minutes. Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. When melted, add celery, onion, and herbs. Season with salt and pepper and cook until the onions are translucent, about 7 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.

Grease your Crock-Pot bowl and add the toasted bread. Pour the vegetable mixture, eggs, broth, and parsley over the bread. Toss to combine and cover.

Cook on low for 3 to 4 hours, stirring after 2 hours have passed. Garnish with parsley before serving.

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Thanksgiving is hectic; we get it. This is the perfect dish to set aside while you prepare everything else. After the 3-hour cook time, switch the pot to the "keep warm" setting—just give it a stir every 30 minutes or so to make sure the bread around the edges doesn't dry out. If the stuffing is ready hours before dinner time, you can add up to ¼ cup of broth every few hours to keep things hydrated.
